transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 09:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m | Recording ID: ff-2026-03-04-lunaris-sync-57
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Sofia Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Redwood SE), Anika Bose (Redwood CSM); Rajesh Iyer (Lunaris Head of ML), Maya Chen (Lunaris SRE), Tom Alvarez (CTO), Leah Park (Data Eng)

[00:00] Liam: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump into the numbers from last week's run.
[00:15] Rajesh: Yep, Rajesh here. Maya, Tom, Leah on my side.
[00:22] Sofia: Sofia here. I've got the benchmark results to share, a quick deck, and then we can dig into tokens per second per dollar.
[00:35] Liam: Cool, I'll start high-level. Reminder of success criteria: latency p95 under 400ms for 128 token responses, cost target of less than $0.0009 per generated token (target internal), and reliability at 99.9%.
[00:50] Tom: That cost target is aggressive but reflects our unit economics for the product. We're particularly sensitive to inference cost because we'll be doing heavy batching at scale.
[01:10] Sofia: Okay so quick recap of what we ran: 1) Hosted Redwood model (r-ver-1) baseline, no caching, batch size 1 and 4; 2) Hosted with prefix KV caching enabled for repeated prompts (approx 30% cache hit observed in their sample); 3) Dedicated pool run with quantized variant (int8) and batching 8.
[01:35] Leah: Small note - our trace sample skewed toward short contexts, ~70% under 64 tokens. We cleaned but wanted to flag distribution.
[01:45] Sofia: Good call. That affects the tokens/sec since shorter contexts are throughput-friendly.
[01:52] -- slide click noise --
[02:05] Sofia: Baseline hosted, batch1: tokens/sec ~220, p50 latency 160ms, p95 470ms, cost per 1k tokens about $1.05 (so per-token about $0.00105). This exceeds your cost target.
[02:30] Rajesh: p95 470ms is high vs our 400ms, any idea why?
[02:35] Sofia: A couple factors: cold KV cache buildup, and the model variant selection - hosted default routed to r-ver-1 which is higher quality but less optimized. Also network egress and region differences add 50-80ms.
[02:50] Maya: We're in eu-west-1 primarily, correct? We saw some cross-region hops in the logs.
[02:55] Liam: Yes, initial routing was to us-west-2 due to capacity; we'll pin region in the next run.
[03:05] Sofia: Hosted batch4 improved tokens/sec to ~680, p50 210ms, p95 390ms, cost per 1k tokens dropped to ~$0.45 (per-token 0.00045) because batching amortizes overhead.
[03:25] Tom: So batching helps cost but effect on latency is mixed. For interactive use p95 matters more.
[03:35] Sofia: Exactly. For 128 token case, batch4 hit your p95 target at ~390ms but that assumes we can accept slight queuing. If tail latency spikes during bursts, we need fallback.
[03:50] Jared: For dedicated pool with int8 quant and batching 8 we saw tokens/sec ~1400, p50 120ms, p95 260ms, cost per 1k tokens estimated ~$0.22 (per-token 0.00022) given reserved capacity assumptions. That gets well under your cost target.
[04:15] Rajesh: Interesting - do those dedicated numbers include the reserved capacity amortization and our projected utilization?
[04:20] Jared: These are modeled at 75% util; reserved committed pricing rolled in. If your utilization is lower, unit cost will rise - we included a sensitivity table.
[04:35] Leah: What's the caching saving we observed? You said ~30% cache hit in hosted, how did that translate to cost?
[04:42] Sofia: With 30% prefix cache hits, effective tokens generated fell roughly 25% overall because some responses were shorter or reused. In hosted batch4 that pushed cost per 1k tokens from $0.45 to $0.34 in the sample. With dedicated + caching savings stack, we project down to ~$0.16 per 1k tokens.
[05:05] Tom: Does that caching number assume ideal prefix matching or fuzzy matches? Our prompts mutate slightly.
[05:12] Sofia: It's mostly exact prefix matches in this dataset; we recommend running a fuzzy-prefix experiment. We saw diminishing returns when token-level edits exceed ~8 tokens. We'll need representative traces.
[05:25] Rajesh: We'll send anonymized traces after scrub - typical user flows plus a sample of A/B test prompts.
[05:30] Leah: Also note we have some PII in a subset of traces, will scrub.
[05:35] Liam: Great. On batching tradeoffs - recommended approach: dynamic batching with latency SLO guardrails (e.g., if queueing exceeds 20ms then flush). That preserves p95 while getting batching gains.
[05:50] Maya: Is that feature available in hosted or only dedicated?
[05:55] Jared: Dynamic batching is in the runtime - available in hosted with certain limits, fully tunable on Dedicated and Private. For hosted we can expose queue thresholds but not modify kernel-level scheduling.
[06:10] Tom: We also want deterministic cost modeling for execs. Can you put the assumptions in the sheet? e.g., token distribution, util%, reserved commit size, cache hit rate ranges.
[06:20] Liam: Yes we'll update the spreadsheet to include low/medium/high scenarios (cache hit 10/30/50%, util 50/75/90%, batch sizes 1/4/8) and show per-token USD and tokens/sec.
[06:35] Sofia: Quick note on quantization: int8 gave notable perf, but quality regressions are visible on our longer-context summarization tests. For shorter responses it's mostly OK. We can run a targeted eval on your prompt set.
[06:55] Rajesh: That's crucial - quality drop for summaries would be a dealbreaker. How do you recommend we measure quality degradation quantitatively?
[07:05] Sofia: We'll run automated diff-based metrics (ROUGE, BLEU where appropriate) plus human eval on a 200-sample subset. Put a threshold you'd accept, and we'll tune quant profile.
[07:20] Leah: Also curious about model fallback - if quantized route fails quality checks, can runtime route to full-precision variant?
[07:28] Jared: Yes, smart routing policy can fallback to higher-fidelity variant; you'd pay more for that request but keep reliability. We can implement per-route policies.
[07:40] Tom: Security quick check - we need audit logs and KMS support if we go Dedicated/Private. Any blockers?
[07:48] Liam: No blockers; Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations, SSO/SAML and full audit logs. We'll share SOC2 docs again.
[07:58] Anika: I'll attach the security pack to the follow-up email.
[08:02] Maya: For a private trial, how long to stand up an on-prem or VPC deployment? We have infra windows in mid-March.
[08:12] Jared: For a VPC-hosted private trial we can provision in ~2 weeks; on-prem longer. For mid-March we'd recommend VPC private trial in your cloud account.
[08:22] Rajesh: Good. Back to cost - what about burst pricing? We expect erratic traffic.
[08:28] Liam: Dedicated offers burst capacity configuration; cost model includes nominal burst unit cost. Also automatic fallback to hosted for spikes can reduce need for huge reserved commit. We'll show a hybrid scenario.
[08:40] Leah: Any notes on tokenization differences? Our frontend pre-tokenizes some inputs. Will that change numbers?
[08:46] Sofia: Yes pre-tokenization helps; we saw ~5-7% variation across tokenizers. We'll align on tokenization rules when you send traces.
[08:55] Tom: Are there any competitor tradeoffs we should be aware of? We looked at Anthropic and Lambda Labs for on-prem.
[09:00] Liam: Anthropic has strong safety tooling but higher unit cost in our benchmarks; Lambda Labs is cheaper on raw GPU but lacks unified routing and fallback features. We'll include competitor row in the sheet.
[09:15] Rajesh: Good. Let's recap next steps.
[09:20] Liam: Recap: 1) Redwood share updated cost model (Liam) by Friday; 2) Sofia runs controlled benchmarks (Sofia) and provides logs by 3/11; 3) Lunaris shares anonymized traces (Rajesh) by 3/8; 4) schedule private trial for week of 3/22 (Jared to propose).
[09:40] Tom: Sounds good. One more ask - can we get a small sample of the live debug logs (sanitized) showing caching hits and batching queue metrics?
[09:50] Sofia: Yes I'll include those in the deliverable.
[09:55] Liam: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with attachments and calendar invite for the deeper run.
[10:02] Rajesh: Thanks all.
[10:05] End of recording.
